title: Science and research — core set
titleVi: Khoa học và nghiên cứu — bộ từ cốt lõi
description: Bộ từ mô tả cách một nghiên cứu được thiết kế, kiểm chứng và công bố. Nhóm này giúp bạn viết về khoa học mà không rơi vào những câu chung chung kiểu "science is important".
ieltsUse: Dùng cho Task 2 các đề về đầu tư nghiên cứu, đạo đức khoa học, thử nghiệm trên người và vai trò của bằng chứng trong hoạch định chính sách.

words.def: a proposed explanation to be tested by evidence
words.example: The hypothesis was rejected after two independent teams failed to reproduce the result.

words.vi: có ý nghĩa thống kê (không phải do ngẫu nhiên)
words.def: unlikely to have occurred by chance alone
words.example: The improvement was statistically significant, so the programme was extended nationwide.

words.def: the set of methods used in a piece of research
words.example: Reviewers criticised the methodology because participants were not randomly assigned.

words.def: assessment of research by independent experts before publication
words.example: Peer review filters weak studies, although it cannot detect every case of fraud.

words.def: the number of participants in a study
words.example: A sample size of thirty students is far too small for general conclusions.

words.def: a factor that can change and affect a result
words.example: Researchers controlled for income as a variable when comparing exam results.

words.def: a statistical relationship between two things
words.example: There is a strong correlation between sleep duration and academic performance.

words.def: the relationship in which one thing causes another
words.example: Correlation is not causation, so the link may run in the opposite direction.

words.vi: sự lặp lại nghiên cứu để kiểm chứng
words.def: repetition of a study to check its findings
words.example: Without replication, a single striking result should be treated with caution.

words.vi: tính hiệu lực, độ giá trị
words.def: the extent to which a study measures what it claims to
words.example: The validity of the survey was undermined by leading questions.

words.def: an important discovery or advance
words.example: The vaccine was hailed as a breakthrough after decades of failed attempts.

words.def: money awarded to fund a research project
words.example: Competition for a research grant now favours large established laboratories.

words.def: a test of a treatment on human volunteers
words.example: The drug failed its final clinical trial because of unexpected side effects.

words.def: a harmless treatment given to a control group
words.example: Half the volunteers received a placebo so that expectations could be measured.

words.def: the general agreement of experts in a field
words.example: The scientific consensus on climate change has strengthened over thirty years.

words.def: decided according to research findings rather than opinion
words.example: Evidence-based medicine replaced tradition as the standard in most hospitals.

words.vi: suy rộng, ngoại suy từ dữ liệu đã có
words.def: to estimate unknown values from known data
words.example: It is risky to extrapolate national trends from a small regional survey.

words.def: to spread information widely
words.example: Findings are useless unless researchers disseminate them beyond academic journals.

words.def: the legal right to be the only producer of an invention
words.example: A patent gives the company a monopoly, which pushes up the price of the drug.

words.def: a first working version of a new product
words.example: The first prototype was too heavy, so engineers rebuilt it with carbon fibre.

words.def: concerned with ideas rather than practical application
words.example: The theoretical benefits of fusion are enormous, but commercial reactors remain decades away.

words.def: research aimed at solving a practical problem
words.example: Funding bodies increasingly favour applied research over purely curiosity-driven work.

words.def: something that deviates from what is expected
words.example: The anomaly in the data was dismissed as an error for nearly twenty years.

words.vi: nghiên cứu theo chiều dọc (theo dõi nhiều năm)
words.def: research that follows the same people over a long period
words.example: A longitudinal study tracking 10,000 children found that early reading predicted later income.

words.def: the participants who do not receive the treatment being tested
words.example: The control group improved slightly too, which complicates the interpretation.
